pair.short: Two currencies traded against each other. In EURUSD, you buy or sell euros with US dollars.
pair.example: If EURUSD rises from 1.0800 to 1.0850, the euro has strengthened against the dollar.

buy.short: Opening a position because you expect price to rise. You profit if it rises and lose if it falls.

sell.short: Opening a position because you expect price to fall. You profit if it falls and lose if it rises.

wait.short: Deliberately not opening a position because there's no clear edge yet. Not trading is a decision too.

entry.short: The price at which you open a position. Every profit and loss is measured from here.

pip.short: The smallest standard price move in forex: 0.0001 for most pairs, 0.01 for yen pairs.
pip.example: EURUSD going from 1.0800 to 1.0842 is a 42-pip rise.

posisi.short: A trade that's currently open, buy or sell, until you close it.

spread.short: The gap between the buy and sell price a broker offers. It's a cost you pay every time you open a position.

volatilitas.short: How far and how fast price moves. High volatility means bigger opportunities and bigger risks alike.

likuiditas.short: How easily something can be bought or sold without moving the price much. Major pairs like EURUSD are very liquid.

candlestick.short: One bar on the chart that sums up the open, close, high and low price for one period.
candlestick.example: On the H4 timeframe, one candle represents 4 hours of price movement.

body.short: The thick part of a candle, from the open to the close. A long body means one side clearly won that period.

sumbu.short: The thin lines above and below the body: price reached there but didn't hold until the candle closed.

timeframe.short: How much time one candle represents. M15 = 15 minutes, H1 = 1 hour, H4 = 4 hours, D1 = 1 day.

h4.short: The 4-hour timeframe: each candle sums up 4 hours of price. Every Trading Game question uses H4.

trend.short: The general direction of price over a stretch of time: up (higher highs and lows), down, or sideways.

menyamping.short: Price moving back and forth between two limits with no clear direction. Often the best time to WAIT.

kemiringan.short: How steep a trend is, measured as average pips per candle. Positive means up, negative means down.

support.short: A price area where declines have stalled and bounced several times. The more often it's touched, the more the market watches it.
support.example: In the Trading Game, support is drawn as a dashed green band.

resistance.short: A price area where rallies have stalled and turned down several times. The opposite of support.
resistance.example: In the Trading Game, resistance is drawn as a dashed red band.

rentang.short: The distance between the lowest and highest price over a period. “At 80% of the range” means near the top.

breakout.short: When price pushes convincingly through support or resistance. A false breakout (fakeout) quickly falls back inside.

konfirmasi.short: An extra sign that backs your idea before you get in, for example a candle closing above resistance after a breakout.

pin-bar.short: A candle with a small body and a long wick on one side: a sign price was rejected from that area.

penolakan.short: Price touches a level and is quickly pushed back, leaving a long wick.

bullish.short: Leaning up. A bullish candle closes higher than it opened.

bearish.short: Leaning down. A bearish candle closes lower than it opened.

stop-loss.short: A price limit that closes a losing position automatically. You decide how big a loss you'll accept before you get in.

take-profit.short: A target price that closes a winning position automatically.

risk-reward.short: The distance to your stop loss compared with the distance to your take profit. 1:2 means risking 20 pips for a 40-pip target.

leverage.short: Borrowing from a broker to make a position bigger. Profits and losses grow by the same multiple.

margin.short: The deposit a broker holds while a leveraged position is open.

diversifikasi.short: Spreading risk across several assets or ideas so one mistake doesn't take everything.

crypto.short: Digital assets recorded on a blockchain rather than issued by a central bank. Examples: Bitcoin and Ethereum.

blockchain.short: A transaction ledger copied across many computers at once, so it's hard to change quietly.

bitcoin.short: The first crypto (2009), with a maximum supply of 21 million coins set in its network rules.

altcoin.short: Any crypto other than Bitcoin. Generally more volatile and riskier.

stablecoin.short: A crypto designed to track the value of another asset, usually the US dollar. How stable it is depends on its issuer's reserves.

wallet.short: Where you keep the keys to your crypto. Whoever holds the keys (the seed phrase) controls the assets.

seed-phrase.short: A set of 12 or 24 words that restores a wallet. Never share it with anyone, including an “admin”.

exchange.short: A platform for buying and selling crypto. Choose one that's officially registered in your country.

fomo.short: Fear of missing out: rushing in after price has already run a long way.

overtrading.short: Opening too many positions, usually out of boredom or to win back a loss. Costs and mistakes pile up.

jurnal-trading.short: A record of every decision: why you got in, what happened, and the lesson. The simplest way to stop repeating mistakes.
